name: manual_e3c883
claim: Before committing a pinned npx or npm version (pkg@X.Y.Z), prove it exists with 'npm view <pkg> versions --json' and check its age with 'npm view <pkg> time': a pin proposed by a subagent or pasted from notes can be invented, and a non-existent pin makes npx fail for every MCP entry that uses it. When sessions disagree on a real version, the recorded PT decision wins (mcp-remote@0.1.43, DECISIONS.md 2026-08-22), so read it before choosing. Repeat the check whenever a pin crosses a handoff.

decisions.notes: orama-system#421, 2026-10-18: a reviewer-nitpick fix pinned mcp-remote@0.1.10, which is not on the registry (123 versions; 0.1.10 absent; 0.1.43, 0.14.3 and 0.15.1 exist). A parallel session independently chose 0.14.3 ('newest release at least two weeks old'); the operator's later edit set both Exa and Firecrawl entries to 0.1.43 per the PT decision. The invented string reappeared in a later relayed message. Third-party mirrors lagged the live registry, which is authoritative for what npx resolves. Complements the existing rule to pin reviewed versions and never use @latest.
